0 · What is a Kubernetes cluster?

Region: EU West
physical cloud location
contains →
Kubernetes Cluster A
control plane + worker nodes
contains →
Nodes
CPU · RAM · network · storage
run →
Namespaces → Deployments → Pods
A cluster is the infrastructure boundary where Kubernetes schedules and manages applications. Pods consume resources supplied by its worker nodes.
Multi-cluster: companies may run separate clusters per region, environment, business domain or failure boundary. The application stack is commonly deployed to each cluster; data replication and failover are designed separately.

4 · Horizontal vs vertical scaling

Horizontal: add more Pods
Vertical: larger CPU/RAM per Pod
High read traffic → scale horizontally
Heavier crypto/SDK work → larger Pod
Use VPA recommendations carefully for vertical sizing; HPA handles changing replica counts. Load tests and SLOs determine real values.

7 · Payment provider, retries and refunds

Payment Service
idempotency key
⇄
External Provider
charge + webhook
→
Inbox / Reconciliation Worker
verify final state
READY Waiting for scenario…
Do not trust a timeout as failure. The provider may have charged successfully after your connection broke. Store the attempt, query provider status or consume its signed webhook, deduplicate events, and run a periodic reconciliation worker. Refund is a new idempotent operation with its own state—not deletion of the original payment.
